turnaround_reason: Acetyl/engineered-materials demand trough plus a debt overhang from the ~$11B DuPont M&M acquisition crushed the stock from ~$71 to ~$46. Recovery thesis is a sequential acetyl-chain rebound, price increases sticking, and free cash flow directed at deleveraging.
bullish_points: Q2 2026 beat (reported EPS 2.45 vs 2.22 est, +10%); management guided 2H toward ~$3.00 EPS and raised FY FCF outlook to $700-800M
Cheap on forward earnings: fwd P/E ~7.4, EV/EBITDA ~9.8, P/B ~1.2, trading near 52w low ($45.8 vs low $35 / high $71)
Acetyl price hikes implemented; SharpCell carbon-capture binder partnership adds an optionality kicker
Analyst target mean $63.6 (~39% upside) with 16 analysts; positive FCF ($950M TTM) funds deleveraging
Dividend slashed to $0.03/qtr — a credible signal that all cash is going to the balance sheet, not defended-for-optics
bearish_points: Very high leverage: total debt ~$12.4B, D/E 270, net-debt/EBITDA ~4.8x — highly sensitive to rates and a demand relapse
TTM profit margin negative (-12%); no trailing P/E because bottom line is still red on impairment/interest drag
Structural overcapacity and weak auto/industrial end-market demand in both acetyl and engineered materials
Recovery is a management projection, not yet demonstrated across a full year — execution risk on both price realization and volume
catalyst: Continued sequential acetyl-chain earnings recovery and visible deleveraging progress on the Q3 print
suggested_trade: Small-to-medium starter spot $44-46; scale on a confirmed deleveraging trajectory. Long-dated calls (Jan 2027) reasonable for those wanting leverage given IV, but the debt makes spot the cleaner expression.
key_risk: A demand relapse or credit-market tightening that stalls deleveraging and forces refinancing at higher rates — with this much leverage, equity is the thin tranche.
would_skip_if: Acetyl pricing rolls back over, FCF guidance is cut, or net-debt/EBITDA fails to improve on the Q3 print.
